title: How AbstractQueuedSynchronizer works
context: What is AQS, and how do locks like ReentrantLock use it?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: AbstractQueuedSynchronizer is a framework for building locks and synchronizers. It keeps an integer `state` updated with CAS, and a FIFO queue of waiting threads. To acquire, a thread tries to change state; if that fails it enqueues itself and parks. Release changes state and unparks the next queued thread. A subclass defines what the state means: ReentrantLock uses it as a hold count, Semaphore as permits, CountDownLatch as the remaining count. Shared and exclusive modes are both supported.

points.title: State and CAS
points.why: The synchronizer's state is changed atomically. Success means the thread owns the resource.

points.title: FIFO wait queue
points.why: Threads that fail to acquire wait in a queue and are parked until released.

points.title: Subclasses define meaning
points.why: Locks, semaphores and latches all reuse the same queue with different state rules.
